_: ONE table, read by both halves of the standup's model reading (docs/modules/solitaire-agile.md): an object of named sections, each a list of rows with a name. lookup asks the model object -- Scripts/Get-PromptFileStatus.ps1 Get-P20ModelObject (tkTestToolkit -Rituals) and agent/core/models.py model_object() (Tests/test_rituals.py) -- for an id and a session id. expected null is no object: an empty or missing id, or an id of consts.json models.notModels, is not a model, known or unknown. Otherwise the object is {id, sessionId, name, family, known}: id is the row's id as written, sessionId the row's sessionId (null when the row has none or it is empty). A row whose expected.known is true takes name and family from the shipped model map's OWN row for the id (Config/models.json, consts.json models.file), so the table does not move when a row is added or a name is changed; both suites first assert the id has a row there, and a row with retired true also asserts that the map's current block names some other id for its family. A row whose expected.known is false states name and family outright: the id as written and null, because an id is looked up and never parsed -- the ids are made up, and both suites assert the map has no row for them, so a model added later cannot collide with one. An id is matched exactly, case and all, as the map lookup (Get-P20ModelInfo, model_info) matches it today. If the two halves ever disagree about a row, one of them is wrong.

lookup.name: a known id takes its name and family from its row
another provider's known id, from its own row
a retired id the map keeps is known, not unknown
an unknown id reads as written, with no family
an unknown id holding a family word is not that family
an id is matched exactly, case and all

an empty sessionId is no session
an empty id is not a model
a missing id is not a model

_sessions: The session reader's four sections, read by Scripts/Standup-Rules.ps1 Read-P20StandupSessions and its rules (tkTestToolkit -Rituals) and agent/solitaire/sessions.py (Tests/test_rituals.py). inside drives the pure path rule (Test-P20PathInside, path_inside): a cwd and roots in, true or false out -- separators either way, a Windows root (a drive letter, or a share) compared ignoring case and any other root ordinal, and a folder that only shares a root's name as a prefix is not inside. porcelain drives the pure parse of `git worktree list --porcelain` (ConvertFrom-P20WorktreePorcelain, parse_worktree_porcelain): the text in, the working folders out in its order, a bare entry left out. sessions is a scratch Claude Code projects folder per row: files maps a path under the projects folder to its lines, or to { mtime, lines } where mtime is the file's last write as a UTC instant (each suite sets it after writing: [System.IO.File]::SetLastWriteTimeUtc, os.utime); with no mtime a file is last written at the row's asOf. A line is a SPEC in the style of Tests/fixtures/usage/cases.json, rendered by each suite into a Claude Code line: t is the line's timestamp, written as given; sid its sessionId (left out when absent); cwd its working folder (left out when absent); model message.model; type the line's type (assistant when absent); side the subagent flag; raw a line written as it is. Every rendered line carries the content text below as its message text, so privacy can look for it. The roots are the row's checkout, then its worktrees, then the folders its porcelain text lists (the parse above), and the reader runs over [window.since, window.asOf]. expected is every {id, sessionId} pair, in the reader's order: by id, then by sessionId, ordinal. privacy holds rules every sessions row's output must meet: keys, the only keys a pair may carry; strings, no needle and no path segment (four characters or more) of the row's checkout, worktrees, porcelain folders, cwd values or project folder names (each also split on '-') anywhere in the output, ignoring case -- and both suites first assert that no such string is part of an expected id or sessionId, so the check cannot pass by accident.
content: a prompt the reader must never keep

_seats: The seats reader's section, read by Scripts/Standup-Rules.ps1 Get-P20StandupOrgSeats (tkTestToolkit -Rituals) and agent/solitaire/org_seats.py standup_seats (Tests/test_rituals.py). A row is a whole org.json (org; absent is no file), a Space slug (space) and teamAgile (true when absent). Each suite hands org to the org chart's OWN reader -- Read-P20OrgChart over a scratch hub, read_org_chart over the text -- and the reader's result to the seats reader, so the chart's validity verdict is the reader's and never re-checked; a row with invalid also asserts the reader's kind. expected is the seats, in the chart's order (its positions in tree order, each position's seats in file order), each {seat, position, model}, model the model object with a null sessionId. A model is stated the way the lookup rows state one, so the table does not move when a model row is added: {id} is an id the shipped map has a row for, named and grouped by that row, known; {current} is a key of the map's current block, the id it names today (both suites assert the id has a row); {id, known: false} is an id the map has no row for and no current key names ignoring case, named as written with no family. A seat's model is free text read by lookup: an id with a row, matched exactly; else a current key, matched ignoring case as a worker size is (Get-P20ModelForSize, current_model); else the text as written. Only a seat whose space is the slug exactly, that names a model and no person, is seated: a vacant seat (the chart's rule -- no model is vacant, and the position's defaultModel does not fill it), a person's seat, a pool, another Space's seat and an org-wide seat (no space) add nobody. Privacy, over every row: a seat carries seat, position and model and nothing else, a model the model object's five keys, and no machine or person value of the row's org (its trees' machines, its seats' machine and person) appears in the output, ignoring case -- and both suites first assert that no such value is part of the row's expected seats, so the check cannot pass by accident.

a seat naming a model and a person is the person's, and adds nobody
a pool adds nobody

_join: The join's section, read by Scripts/Standup-Rules.ps1 Join-P20StandupMembers (tkTestToolkit -Rituals) and agent/solitaire/room_join.py join_members (Tests/test_rituals.py). A row is today's members as the fill builds them -- labelled (the labelled workers), members (the members the cards name that no label routes to, each with its plate) and engineer (null for a fill with none) -- and cards (the model ids the cards in play name; an empty one is skipped), seats (each a seat's free-text model, which each suite turns into the seats reader's {seat, position, model} by that reader's own lookup, Resolve-P20SeatModelId and seat_model_id) and sessions (the session reader's {id, sessionId} pairs, as it returns them). expected.source is seats+sessions, sessions, seats or room; expected.unknown the ids the map has no row for, sorted. expected.members is the output in its order -- today's record and the added members in label order, then the engineer -- each {label, name, empty, record, session, models} and its plate where the row states one: name is the default naming's (today's: the tracker's word, a card member's family with a capital, an unknown id as written), nameMap the map naming's where it differs (a card, seat or session member named by its most recent model: the id the map's current block names for the family when the member has it, else its last id in id order); models are {id, sessionId} in id order, each a model object whose name, family and known both suites take from the lookup itself (Get-P20ModelObject, model_object), sessionId the ordinally last session that shows the id, else null -- the reader's pairs carry no time, and its privacy rule keeps them to two keys. record is false for a member only a seat or a session adds (in the round, never in the record), session whether a session shows it. Over every row both suites also assert that each input member comes back with every field it had, in the same order, and only models, session and record added; where expected.source is room, the members ARE today's record, and every case of standup-team.json run through the join with no seat and no session gives back its fill's record the same way.

a retired id from a session: known, the family's member, named by its own row
a card member whose card names a worker and no model id keeps its name under both namings

a session line that is not a model adds nobody, and the source stays the room

_room: The seating's section: standup-team.json's room rows with one tier more, read by Get-P20StandupRoomSeats (tkTestToolkit -Rituals), standup.room_seats (Tests/test_rituals.py) and the stage (web/src/modules/solitaireAgile/stage/seats.test.ts), in the same shape. A label row may say session true: a session shows that member. The seats go to the engineer, then the members with work, then the idle members a session shows, then the other idle members, each run in label order, then the invented cast members in grid order; never by usage. present, round (label, cast, window) and desks are the expected answer, as in standup-team.json. A row with join names a join row: both suites run that row's join and assert that its members, seated -- the engineer the last, the rest as {label, empty, session} -- are this row's engineer and labels. The room's rules hold over every row: the size picked is the size seen, everyone seated has a turn, the empty desks are only the windows past the size, the engineer sits first, and a member a session shows is a real member (cast false).
